To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“stress induces mast cell activation in the skin through NGF-dependent pathways”.
stress can precipitate or aggravate skin disorders and that the precise mechanisms leading to these stress-induced or aggravated skin disorders have just started to be understood.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the neuroendocrine regulation of the skin and its disorders.
the neuroendocrine mechanisms of the brain–skin connection, and how they can be modulated to improve the efficacy of treatment of stress-related skin disorders.
the neurobiologic and neuroendocrine mechanisms of stress-induced and -aggravated skin disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
stress can trigger or aggravate certain neuroinflammatory manifestations in peripheral tissues including the skin.
the stress system, including NGF and mast cells, is an important player in the pathogenesis of skin diseases.
stress-induced neuroinflammatory skin disorders are mediated by the brain–skin connection, which is regulated by NGF and involves mast cells and their mediators, suchas SP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stress system is involved in the development and aggravation of skin diseases.
stress is associated with the activation of mast cells and the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines.
the stress-induced skin disorders are mediated by mast cells, which are activated by CRH and sensory neuropeptides, such as SP and CGRP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the skin is a very important organ for the stress response.
the skin can respond to stress in a manner that is similar to how the brain does.
the skin is a target for the stress response.
